extraction.status: Activation-gated owner CLI and detached one-shot worker implemented. Extraction stays inert until the owner runs `shadowgraph activate extraction`; fixtures are not real-host activation evidence.
extraction.hostProfile: Windows Claude Code 2.1.288. Unknown versions and other platform policy sources block; synthetic portability tests are not host activation evidence.
extraction.route: Existing claude.ai first-party subscription sign-in only. No keys, helper, proxy/provider environment, alternate model or paid fallback.
extraction.restrictions: No tools, instruction files, hooks, MCP, plugins, skills, memory or session persistence; empty transient cwd outside repositories; explicit environment; managed policy conflicts block without disabling safeguards.
extraction.evidenceLevel: Documented switches plus bounded local version/help/auth/doctor checks. These checks do not establish real invocation confinement, stdin/schema behavior or the no-overage condition: the owner verifies them on the installed host before activating extraction, and the no-overage condition is the owner's assertion, which ShadowGraph cannot detect.
extraction.limits: Input 256 KiB; inline schema 64 KiB; combined child output 512 KiB; invocation 120 seconds; each diagnostic 10 seconds. Unknown terminal results block without retry.
extraction.hostBookkeeping: The host may refresh its own subscription credentials and bookkeeping despite session persistence being disabled. ShadowGraph never reads or records credentials.

versionPolicy: The delivery evidence is bound to this host and version. Another host or version is unverified until its own receipt. The version is read at activation and recorded there; the delivered head reports it as verified or unverified, and a host that updates after activation stays recorded as it was until the next activation.
sameTurnGap: Delivery reaches the model at a session's start and at each prompt. Nothing reaches it within a turn: what is recorded during a turn is available from the next prompt or session on. The only demonstrated same-turn mechanism is a blocking hook, which is never adopted.

capture.status: integrated and inert: nothing is captured until the owner activates capture after AG-2
capture.hostFields: from the host's hooks reference (read 2026-09-30); a field a payload lacks falls back as each event row declares, and no field is assumed present on a version this manifest does not verify. The transcript's entry format is not documented at all (the host says it is internal and changes between versions): the cursor reads it as a hypothesis AG-2 confirms, and stops reading a session at the first line it does not recognise

events.identity: message_id when the payload carries one; otherwise (a prompt_id, which capture does not read, does not count) the session's occurrence ordinal, which is not exact
events.observation: role user and the working directory

events.material: the tool's name, then every leaf of tool_input and tool_response labelled by its path, each string with its own line breaks
events.identity: tool_use_id, which is exact; without one, the session's occurrence ordinal, which is not exact
events.observation: the tool's name and the working directory; an outcome observed only as a success, from a Bash or PowerShell exit_code of 0 for a single command, otherwise absent, and none at all for a call without a tool_use_id

events.material: as PostToolUse, with the host's error text, which is never parsed
last_assistant_message; the turn's other assistant text, and all of it when the Stop carries no final message, arrives through the transcript cursor, which reads at every Stop
events.identity: the session's occurrence ordinal: the host documents no turn number
events.observation: role assistant; stop_reason is not recorded; a Stop whose final message repeats the session's previous Stop is marked possibleDuplicateOf

events.material: none of its own: it triggers the transcript cursor's read before the host compacts
none of its own: the transcript cursor's last read, best effort within the host's SessionEnd budget
events.identity: none: it records no item; the session's record counts its ends

events.material: the assistant's text blocks read from the session's transcript (transcript_path) by the cursor at Stop, PreCompact and SessionEnd, from where the session was first captured onwards; never a thinking block, a tool call or result, a user entry or any other entry (each tool call's name and input are read only to tell ShadowGraph's own calls apart, and never stored)
events.identity: the transcript entry's uuid, exact while the host keeps each entry's uuid unique and stable (a hypothesis AG-2 confirms); a Stop's final message found in the transcript by the Stop's own read or the next (one entry, or a run of entries, compared with its whitespace folded) is that Stop's copy and is not recorded again
events.observation: role assistant; no working directory, tool or outcome, since none is read from an entry

neverCaptured: the model's hidden reasoning, which no hook delivers
anything the host neither delivers to these hooks nor writes to the session's transcript as assistant text: other events, user entries other than the prompt, and subagents' own transcript files
other applications, and anything outside Claude Code
activity in a project not resolved from a worktree binding the store itself recorded (from the directory the hook runs in), or in a project the coverage leaves out
a hook payload over 1 MiB, or one that has not arrived within 3 seconds, which is never read
an event missing what it is captured by: a prompt that is blank, a tool call with no tool name, or any event with no session id

transcript content from before the session's first capture, from before capture was last activated, from a generation of the file the cursor did not read (a rewrite or another file is read from where it was found, never re-scanned), or from a session whose transcript stopped being read
ShadowGraph's own traffic (signals S-1, S-2, S-3), which is counted per session as self-events instead

an item over maxItemBytes, a transient refusal that no view declares (a transcript entry is measured, as a prompt or a Stop is, after ShadowGraph's own delivered blocks are removed, except that one over twice maxItemBytes is refused without stripping)
anything, when the store lies inside a git repository or working tree, when the store cannot be read, or when its lock cannot be taken in time
anything into a SQLite store: delivery reports a SQLite store busy while a capture writes it, so capture writes a JSON store only
the transcript of a session that is ShadowGraph's own: a worker's (S-3), or one whose prompt carried its correlation mark (S-2)
a transcript path that is not an absolute path to a .jsonl file, or that is not a regular file

content the redaction policy removes before write: credential-shaped text is replaced by [REDACTED] before anything is measured, hashed or kept, and an item whose redacted text the credential check still flags is kept with no content (credential_withheld)
declarations: A session one project owns refuses another project's capture (session_in_another_project), and the refused project's reads declare the gap.

possibleDuplicateOf marks an item identified only by its ordinal that repeats the session's previous item of the same event, including a prompt or tool result without a host identifier; a Transcript item, although its uuid identifies it, is marked possibleDuplicateOf the newest Stop or Transcript item of its session holding the same material; it removes nothing, and extraction must never treat it as a reason to skip.

The transcript cursor reconstructs a gap as a period with its bounds (plan section 22.7) only for tool calls: a call the transcript shows, used and answered within one read, that no capture holds and that is not ShadowGraph's own is counted in tool_calls_not_captured, whatever the cause (a failed store, a denied or interrupted call, an admission refusal, a payload over 1 MiB). A prompt lost to a failed store is not reconstructed: message_id has no documented relation to a transcript entry. A lost Stop loses nothing, since the cursor reads its turn.
While extraction is not active, pending capture can fill the queue; expiry or owner deletion can relieve it. capture_limited declares any active ceiling.

tool_response.exit_code is taken from the host's documented fields and is hypothetical until AG-2 confirms it on the installed host; a non-zero status is never observed, since it is not a failure by itself (grep, diff, robocopy and wrappers use it for other results).

Every event at the six hooks, in every directory, runs a synchronous hook and adds its latency, bounded by a 5 000 ms deadline (8 000 ms for a write already inside the store); the cursor reads under the store's lock, at most 4 MiB of new lines (and one line of up to 8 MiB) at a time, and records nothing more once too little time is left. SessionEnd runs within the host's SessionEnd budget, which the template's 10-second timeout raises. It is measured and declared at AG-2.

A capture that cannot take the store's lock in time, or has too little time left to commit, writes nothing, there or anywhere else, and is not counted: a tool call lost this way is reconstructed (tool_calls_not_captured) when the transcript shows it used and answered within one read, after the anchor; a Stop's turn is still read by the cursor, and a prompt lost this way leaves no record. The AG-2 approval text states this with the measured burst loss.

Every item's material and observation are redacted before they are written (redaction at capture, M-2): credential-shaped text, and whatever a credential-named key, a pair keyed by one or a pair whose first names one holds in a tool's input or response, is replaced by [REDACTED]. An item whose redacted text the credential check still flags -- as it stands, folded, or in a JSON string it carries -- or that holds a private key's boundary line is kept blocked (credential_withheld), with no content and no hash, and stays queued until it is deleted or expires. Redaction can over-reach (prose naming a password field); a secret used as an object key is caught only in a known shape; a token glued after an underscore in a tool name is not; a delivered block under a credential-named key is removed without being counted as S-1; a private key split across separate hook events is withheld only by its boundary lines, though one split across the transcript entries one read records is redacted whole. A Stop whose text is withheld is recorded again, withheld, from its transcript copy, and a run of transcript entries whose joined text the check flags is withheld entry by entry, when its entries are read together, when a withheld Stop holds the run for the rest of its copy, or when time cuts it; a run that a read with no Stop waiting divides (a PreCompact between its entries) is judged in parts. Redaction is pattern-based: it does not recognise short or attached flags (-p<value>), a value separated from its name by whitespace alone (a netrc's password <value>, prose such as 'my password is ...'), cookies passed as arguments (curl -b), names that are not credential words (DB_PASS, SSHPASS), one-time codes in URLs, or a secret written as prose; the AG-2 approval text names these. Host identifiers (session, message and tool-call ids) are stored as the host gave them.

A capture refused because the store lies inside a repository, or because the store cannot be loaded, writes nothing; while delivery is active on the same store, delivery's processing line reports capture unavailable with the reason (store_inside_repository, store_unreadable, newer_schema, deletion_pending), found without any write.

While the store holds a pending deletion record, capture writes nothing; the next write by another verb completes it when this build can complete it, and otherwise every write refuses until a retained file of the failed restore is put back.
Turning capture off disables it first, then attempts bounded cleanup and closes store-limit episodes. Locked, unreadable or pending stores leave cleanup explicitly deferred; capture stays disabled.

The capture store is written owner-only (0600; FND-P6-11), whatever mode it had, and its lock and any directory its fence makes are owner-only too; a manual store keeps its mode, or is owner-only when new. On Windows the mode maps only the read-only bit, and privacy rests on the profile folder's access control, which AG-2 checks. A JSON restore's temporary and rollback files take the destination's mode; a SQLite restore's own files take the process default (capture writes a JSON store only).
uninstall-hooks from a build before the capture hook (such as the runtime pinned at AG-1) does not recognise capture handlers and leaves them installed; roll back from a runtime that can capture.
The transcript's shape is a hypothesis: the first line it does not recognise stops the session's transcript for good (transcript_unrecognised); the session's hook material is still captured.
A session whose event comes from another project, or from a directory no covered binding resolves, stops being read for good (session_left_project), so no project's text is filed under another's.

The cursor is anchored where the session was first captured, and again at each re-activation of capture (transcript_reanchored) and at each rewrite or new file (transcript_rewritten): what was written between the last read and the anchor is not read. If the host rewrites the file when it compacts, the text written between a compaction and the next read is lost each time; AG-2 records what compaction does.

Uninstalling the capture hooks without deactivating capture pauses it: eligible transcript material is read after reinstallation unless retention, deletion or another persistent cursor refusal blocks that session.

A Stop's final message is reconciled with its transcript copy only by the Stop's own read and the next. If the host's last_assistant_message differs from the entries' text by more than whitespace, the final message is recorded twice, the second marked possibleDuplicateOf the first; AG-2 checks one scratch turn. Both sides are compared redacted, so a credential-named value at a place where the two differ in whitespace can also split them.

A line over 8 MiB is skipped unread and declared (transcript_line_oversized); a session end that leaves lines unread, or a partial last line, is declared (transcript_incomplete_at_end); a SessionEnd that never runs, or is cut short, declares nothing.
Reading, and so the reconstruction of gaps, happens only at Stop, PreCompact and SessionEnd.

The cursor's anchor is an unkeyed SHA-256 of the 64 bytes before its position: where those bytes are message text, a guess at them can be checked against it, redacted text included. AG-2 checks the host's line layout, and the approval text states it.

A merge import with cursor collisions, capture retention state or deletion knowledge refuses; it does not replace a cursor backward or forward. Retention-neutral session collections join by key: merges of pre-reownership counters or independently opened copies of the same origin/session can refuse capture_collection_malformed. Multiple capture.limited entries for one limit can remain after an allowed merge: status aggregates them and a new refusal updates the first. A nonempty deletion registry makes loaded stores carry the merge-refusal flag.

Capture persistence uses a per-store .control.json ledger and .restore.lock restore fence, plus deletion-registry.json and deletion-registry.json.lock in the private ShadowGraph home. These files count in the growth/privacy inventory; hooks and expiry never write the ledger or registry, and automatic retention never deletes them. Restore recovery files may retain removed raw and remain a separate owner decision.

Retention uses positive safe-integer days; computed deadlines cap at the schema timestamp 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z. Restore reports differing destination, backup and effective project windows even when no control write is needed.
Each session keeps its newest 8 transcript gaps and counts the rest.

A session that writes more to its transcript between two reads than a read takes falls behind: a Stop's final message found later than the Stop's own read and the next is recorded again (marked possibleDuplicateOf), a tool call whose use and result fall in different reads is not checked, and a session end with lines left unread declares transcript_incomplete_at_end; AG-2 measures how far behind a real session falls.
Subagent entries the host may write into the main transcript file would be read as the session's own assistant text; AG-2 checks whether it does.
session_left_project starts when the session's event came from another project or an uncovered directory: the owning project's views show that time, never the place.

A transcript missing at the session's first capture, or with no complete line yet, is anchored at its start; a transcript that goes missing later changes nothing until a file is there again, which is then checked like any rewrite. A cursor whose fields are not the shape this build writes (a merge or a hand edit) is never read (transcript_unrecognised).
A build from PR-33 to PR-36c carries a session's cursor and gaps unread and declares no transcript gap: a rollback pin to one under-declares what the transcript cursor did not read.

A cursor keeps a SHA-256 digest of the 64 bytes before its position (at an anchoring, bytes from before the session's first capture or a re-activation), never the bytes: a rewrite is found when the file's path, its length or those 64 bytes change, and one that keeps all three is read on as new.
